rv.q: Overall, Aftermath feels like one of those long anecdotes where the narrator realizes they left out essential details and suddenly rushes to stick them in at the end.
A journalist himself, Mr. Zax shows a greater flair here for storytelling structure than he does for dialogue.
But “Aftermath,” opening tonight at A.R.T./NY, is too flawed a play for the issues to hit home anywhere near as effectively.
Sadly, by the time it reaches its conclusion, the quartet of actors are spent and so is the audience—and not in a good way.

cn.t: Strong performances can't salvage David Zax's overly ambitious family drama about a journalist's post-Taliban kidnapping recovery, which struggles to balance its weighty themes and fails to make its moral questions resonate.
